questions.question: How do you check if a string is a palindrome in Go?
questions.title: Palindrome Check Go
questions.direct_answer: Two-pointer: compare s[i] and s[j] from both ends, advance inward. First mismatch = false. O(n) time, O(1) space. Verified: "racecar" true, "hello" false.

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The rune-safe version, for the interview completeness: the byte-indexed loop works for ASCII; a multibyte string needs rune-based access (the DSA topic's reverse insight). The safe pattern: convert to []rune, two-pointer over the rune slice, compare — the same O(n)/O(n-for-conversion) as any Unicode handling.

The two-pointer's early exit, quantified: a palindrome check on a string that fails at position 0 returns after ONE comparison — the algorithm's best case is O(1). The reverse-and-compare always does the full O(n) reverse. The performance folklore: two-pointer's early exit matters on adversarial input (random strings that rarely are palindromes — the common case for a filter).

The circular palindrome / longest-substring-palindrome extensions (Manacher's algorithm, expand-around-center) — the two-pointer base case is the primitive those build on. The interview flow: two-pointer first (correct, optimal), the extensions if the role is algorithm-heavy.
